FN-FT69CDD-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 151
Committee: Economic Development and Sponsor: Representative Chris Blackshear
Tourism
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/12/2024
House Bill 151as introduced proposes a constitutional amendment, which if ratified,
would prohibit all forms of gaming in the state, with the exception of certain games authorized
by the Legislature, by general law, including: (1) a state lottery administered by a public
corporation as an instrumentality of the state; (2) casino-style games at no more than seven
licensed gaming establishments; (3) sports wagering; (4) traditional raffles; and (5) traditional
bingo. This bill establishes a gaming commission within the executive branch with a law
enforcement division to police and conduct all gaming activity in the state and eradicate
unlawful gaming activity.
This amendment also requires the Governor to negotiate and execute a compact for Class
III games and sports wagering with the Poarch Band of Creek Indians. In return for negotiating a
compact, the Poarch Band of Creek Indians would be granted one of the seven licenses to
conduct and operate casino-style games outside of lands held in trust.
If ratified, this amendment could result in compact, gaming, license fee, and lottery
revenues to the state depending on the enabling provisions of this amendment as outlined in
House Bill 152 of the 2024 Regular Session.
In addition, this bill will increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from
the State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025.

FN-FT69CDD-4
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 151
Committee: Tourism Sponsor: Representative Chris Blackshear
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/06/2024
House Bill 151 as reported by the Committee on Tourism proposes a constitutional amendment,
which if ratified, would prohibit all forms of gaming in the state, with the exception of certain
games authorized by the Legislature, by general law, including: (1) a state lottery administered
by the newly created Alabama Gambling Commission; (2) pari-mutuel wagering activities at
racetracks in Greene, Jefferson, Macon, and Mobile Counties, at an additional location in
Greene County, and at existing bingo halls in Houston County and Lowndes County; (3)
traditional raffles; and (4) traditional bingo. This bill establishes a gambling commission with a
law enforcement division to police and conduct all gambling activity authorized by this
amendment and eradicate unlawful gaming activity.
This amendment also states the Governor may negotiate and execute a compact for all activities
allowable in this bill with Poarch Band of Creek Indians.
This amendment states that all proceeds from lottery tickets, taxes, and other sources of revenue
of the Commission shall be deposited into an account insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance
Corporation. From this amount, the commission may retain a portion of the proceeds to conduct
lottery games and pay all prizes.
This amendment also levies a tax to be collected by the Department of Revenue between 24 and
32 percent on the net gambling revenues of entities conducting pari-mutuel wagering activities
in lieu of any state or local pari-mutuel taxes which is estimated to be between $99 million and
$132 million to be distributed as follows:
 94% to Gambling Proceeds Fund;
 3% to each county; and
Page 1

 3% to each county; and
FN-FT69CDD-4
 3% to each municipality.
The remaining net lottery proceeds and gaming taxes shall be deposited into the Gambling
Proceeds Fund and appropriated by the Legislature through an independent supplemental
appropriation for ongoing capital improvement and infrastructure projects in existence as of the
ratification of the amendment through March 30, 2029.Thereafter, on an annual basis and
through an independent supplemental appropriation, the first 1% shall be expended on problem
gambling and then the remaining as follows:
 One-third to fund education-related activities;
 One-third to fund non-education, general governmental activities; and
 One-third to the State Department of Transportation.
Operating expenses of the Commission shall be paid from the fund and budgeted and allotted
pursuant to the Budget Management Act. In lieu of any state income taxes owed on the winnings
of any gaming activity, a withholding tax of seven percent on winnings that exceed $500 would
be withheld and credited into a separate sub-account within the Gambling Proceeds Fund. The
amendment also repeals local bingo amendments.
A special election on the amendment would be held on September 14, 2024, at a cost of an
estimated $5 million from the General Fund. The cost of the special election would be repaid to
the General Fund as operating expenses of the Commission.
In addition, this bill will increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the
State General Fund, by an estimated $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025.
